title: The Ink Spots and Ella Fitzgerald show breaks records; Omaha is empty
summary: Cootie's band toured with the Ink Spots and Ella Fitzgerald, broke records in 28 of 29 theatres, with a huge Regal Theatre crowd in a Chicago blizzard, but not in Omaha.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Like, when I was back with the Ink Spots, we had a show with the Ink Spots, Ella Fitzgerald, the Cootie Williams Band and Eddie 'Cleanhead' Vinson, and the Ink Spots. Well, I mean, it was a terrific show and they had a terrific cast,

you know, and we actually broke records in 28 theatres from New York to California. We had 29 theatres to play, and we broke records in 28 theatres. And the theatre we didn't break the record in, you could throw a baseball out there any time and it wouldn't hit nobody. It would have hit nobody, because nobody come to the show! And that was in Nebraska. What's that town in Nebraska?

Omaha. Omaha, Nebraska. They didn't care if it was the Ringling Brothers Circus there; I don't think they would have showed up that week. There was nobody in the theatre. It was strange, because you're used to going in a theatre, people are packing in the theatre, standing in line trying to get in and so forth, and then you come to a theatre and there's nobody around the box office at all. You never see anybody at the box office. Yes, indeed.
Do you think this Omaha thing was a flop... Was it lack of publicity or public relations...?
No, it wouldn't be lack of publicity, because... I don't know. I don't know what it was.
I mean, you must have had a reputation by the time you got there, if you'd broken records in every place....
That's what I'm talking about. If they break records in all the other theatres that they come to...

You know, all the theatres we played, and we played 28 theatres, from New York to California. And believe me, they had some crowds. I have some moving pictures. I'll try to show them to you sometime. I don't know even know if the machine is working now. I couldn't even promise to show them things to you. They was taken so long ago, I don't even know...
I did. I taken moving pictures of the crowds outside some of the theatres, and especially in California, where there were people all around the corner and one-thing-or-another.

Now, we played a theatre in Chicago, the Regal Theatre in Chicago, and the Regal Theatre can seat -- can seat -- over five thousand people. And we were there, we played, and the last night we were there, all week long people are in lines of fours all around the theatre, circle the whole theatre. And they've got some big blocks in Chicago. Long blocks. And they had circled...lines of four people, a four-line... Every show. Every show! And believe me, the weather in Chicago is much worse than the weather in New York. And there was a blizzard going on, and here's all these people outside... That's outside in the street. There's all these people outside trying to get tickets to
come in the theatre. And I mean, they had a blizzard. And when you have a blizzard in Chicago, you got something, because it snows out there. One of them things, I guess.
It was a hot show, though. The show was very good. A very good show.
